answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a verifiable delay function: a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, whose next input depends on the previous result. GPUs may compute separate identities concurrently, but cannot shortcut an individual chain by splitting its steps, so every clone incurs a real time cost. The Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check completion efficiently; the lantern marks the delay, not personhood, and a hollow claim cannot anchor trust without the computation.
